correctness.rationale: The Ore product yields two explicit commutator coefficient equations; for nonzero first coefficient, solve their fixed-field and q-linear conditions to obtain the entire q²Q-element centralizer H(a,b), verify it is abelian and multiplication-closed, and prove these together with J² exhaust maximal commuting sets. Projective line and offset quotient provide uniqueness and complete intersections; cyclic K×/Fq× power-map kernels give the parity incidence. Finite-field norm-equation analysis gives every centralizer multiplicity and swapping the order of counting yields the commuting-pair identity. Independent direct composition tests of four field models and exhaustive maximal clique enumeration for three are executable with included dependency-free verify.py. Exact arithmetic tests are corroboration only; general quantifiers rely on algebraic proof.

Primary literature comparisons distinguish the underlying algebras, graph conventions, and non-implied invariants. value.rationale: Maximal commuting subalgebras and maximal abelian algebra-group subgroups, their intersections, centralizer-size spectra and commuting probability are natural invariants of finite noncommutative local algebras. The classification is complete for an infinite family indexed by any finite field q and extension degree m>=2, and the parity-changing projective incidence geometry supplies structural information beyond an element or orbit count. This is neither arbitrary finite data nor a routine substitution of known tabulations.
